summary: Custom strategy (not a Pine port) — an OVERLAY on top of HODL+DCA rather than a standalone replacement. Sits in cash and only deploys when BTC breaks a new ~100-day high, then rides it out on a wide trailing stop.
logic: Entry (long-only): close > rolling-max of the previous `lookback` closes — i.e. the prior bar's 100-day high is broken on close. On BTC daily that reads as "a new ~3-month high": recent enough to catch regime change, slow enough to avoid most chop.
Exit: trailing stop at peak-since-entry × (1 - trail_pct), evaluated on close rather than intraday low.
trail_pct = 35% is deliberately wide — enough to ride BTC's brutal mid-bull drawdowns without exiting, so it only fires on genuine regime change.
No short logic by design. Shorting into the high is a mean-reversion thesis, which is a different strategy; keeping this one focused.
Leverage 2x. At 3x the liquidation distance (~32%) falls inside the 35% trail, so a deep dip would liquidate before the stop fires.
strengths: Sits in cash until a new ~100-day high, so a prolonged bear market is spent flat instead of held through.
The wide trail keeps risk discipline intact at 2x — the stop fires around -35% from peak, well before the ~-48% liquidation distance.
Long-only and rule-simple: one entry condition, one exit condition, no parameter interaction to overfit.
weaknesses: Backtests do not model funding, which is a meaningful drag on leveraged longs during exactly the bull regimes this strategy holds through.
A 35% trailing stop means giving back a third of the peak before exiting — psychologically hard to hold and a large realised give-back on every exit.
100 daily bars of warmup before the first valid signal after a restart.
Designed against a single 5-year window (2021-05 to 2026-05) with one full bear and one full bull. Regime-dependent by construction, and that sample is thin.
Trades rarely by design, so live confirmation of the edge accumulates very slowly.
